learning: Iteration 4 is the best base. Its failure is excursions (max_error 0.0586 to 0.064 m), not tape loss, and the oval has time margin to slow down. If progress holds with max_error lower, speed was the lever. If progress drops, the robot is now too slow to finish the oval or the course.
notes: Keeps the iteration 4 geometry and lowers base_speed to 1.3 with kd 0.40, so that slower turn entry is the main controller change aimed at the max_error plateau. The oval finish-time margin (1.84 s at 1.5) makes this safe for the 3 s limit.
rationale: Iteration 4 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, kp 4.5, ki 0.25, kd 0.35) is the best design so far: score 188.0, oval progress 0.710, and 3 of 20 oval runs finished. Its line-loss counts (oval 1.2, s-bend 1.0, slalom 1.4) show the span is holding the tape, so I keep the geometry unchanged, as the Builder asked. The remaining failure is off-track excursions: max_error is 0.0586 to 0.064 m against a 0.06 m limit, and 17 of 20 oval runs still leave the track. The oval mean finish time is 1.84 s at base_speed 1.5, so there is time margin under the 3 s limit. Entering turns at lower speed should reduce the lateral excursion without changing the sensing. I therefore lower base_speed from 1.5 to 1.3. On the oval that projects to about 2.1 s, still well within 3 s. I also raise kd from 0.35 to 0.40 to damp the turn-in lag, while keeping kp 4.5 and ki 0.25 so that only speed and derivative damping change. Expected: oval progress at or above about 0.7, max_error nearer 0.055 to 0.06 m, and steering_oscillation near 0.2 to 0.3. If progress falls because the robot is too slow to finish, the base_speed change is the cause and I will restore 1.5.
